# Toolbar

Header: `winui/ui/containers/Toolbar.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/containers/Toolbar.hpp`.

A horizontal strip of commands, usually Buttons, with optional separators between groups.

The items are laid out in a row with 4 DIPs of spacing, like a horizontal [StackControl](stack.md#uistackcontrol). The toolbar itself never takes focus, and each item joins the tab order as in a [StackControl](stack.md#uistackcontrol). There is no overflow handling, so a toolbar wider than its slot overflows like a [StackControl](stack.md#uistackcontrol). For a command bar with an overflow menu, use [ui::CommandBarControl](../controls/command-bar.md#uicommandbarcontrol).

Example: 
```cpp
auto  toolbar = std::make_unique<ui::ToolbarControl>();
auto* cut     = toolbar->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Cut"));
toolbar->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Copy"));
toolbar->add_separator();
toolbar->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Undo"));
cut->on_click([] { /* ... */ });
window.set_content(std::move(toolbar));

// Or declaratively:
window.set_content(ui::Toolbar{
    .content = {
        ui::Button{.text = "Cut", .on_click = [] { /* ... */ }},
        ui::Button{.text = "Copy"},
        ui::Separator{},
        ui::Button{.text = "Undo"},
    },
});
```

## `ui::Toolbar`

A command strip. Builds a [ui::ToolbarControl](#uitoolbarcontrol). Use [ui::Separator](#uiseparator){} between groups.

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::Toolbar{.content = {
    ui::Button{.text = "Open", .on_click = [&] { open_file(); }},
    ui::Separator{},
    ui::Button{.text = "Save", .on_click = [&] { save_document(); }},
}});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Toolbar{
    .spacing, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width,
    .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus,
    .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control, .content
}
```

| <span id="uitoolbar-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uitoolbar-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uitoolbar-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |

## `ui::Separator`

The divider a [Toolbar](#uitoolbar) draws between command groups. Builds a [ui::SeparatorControl](#class-separatorcontrol).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Toolbar{.content = {ui::Button{.text = "Cut"}, ui::Separator{}, ui::Button{.text = "Undo"}}}
```

Derives from `ui::Element`.

A horizontal strip of commands, usually Buttons, with optional separators between groups.

The items are laid out in a row with 4 DIPs of spacing, like a horizontal [StackControl](stack.md#uistackcontrol). The toolbar itself never takes focus, and each item joins the tab order as in a [StackControl](stack.md#uistackcontrol). There is no overflow handling, so a toolbar wider than its slot overflows like a [StackControl](stack.md#uistackcontrol). auto* cut     = toolbar->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Cut"));
toolbar->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Copy"));

toolbar->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Undo"));
cut->on_click([] { /* ... */ });
window.set_content(std::move(toolbar));

Takes ownership of a child, appends it at the end and returns a non-owning observer to it, like [StackControl::add()](stack.md#add).

```cpp
void add_separator()
```

Appends a thin vertical divider line that takes no focus, the same element [make_separator()](#make_separator) returns.

```

The gap between adjacent items in DIPs, 4 by default.

```

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

Visits the internal [StackControl](stack.md#uistackcontrol) that lays the items out.

```cpp

```

Reports the toolbar's items and separators as its direct children. The internal [StackControl](stack.md#uistackcontrol) that [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) visits never appears in the automation tree.

```cpp

```

Exposed to UI Automation as a toolbar.

### make_separator

```cpp
static std::unique_ptr<Element> make_separator()
```

Makes the same separator as a standalone [ui::SeparatorControl](#class-separatorcontrol), for adding it yourself. In a declared child list, write [`ui::Separator{}`](#uiseparator).

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

## class SeparatorControl

Derives from `ui::Element`.

The divider a [Toolbar](#uitoolbar) draws between command groups. It takes no focus, and it is 9 DIPs wide and a control's height. It draws an etched groove, a dark line beside a light one, or a 1 px flat line where the theme draws dividers flat. [ui::Separator](#uiseparator) builds it and [ui::ToolbarControl::add_separator()](#add_separator) adds it.

### SeparatorControl

```cpp
SeparatorControl() = default
```

A separator. It has no state.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

Exposed to UI Automation as a separator.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

A fixed width, and the height of a line of body text plus the theme's padding. It doesn't take the available height, which would make an Auto-sized row holding the toolbar grow.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the groove or the flat line, centered across the width.
